$comment: What a decision must carry to reach its decider in rulable form, rather than as a bare yes/no line in chat. Anchored to standing practice rather than invented: context/options/consequences is Architecture Decision Records (Nygard, 2011); options evaluated against what the situation forces is CMMI DAR's alternatives-against-criteria; carrying the alternatives considered and not just the winner is ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 rationale capture; status moving proposed -> last-call -> decided is IETF-style last call before canonization. A decision record is not a requirement: a requirement is what a party outside the work asked for, and a decision record is what a decider is handed to rule on a choice the work itself produced. It must be readable by a decider who does not hold the repository's state — plain language, no bare internal shorthand — and it must carry nothing below that decider's own altitude: the options and consequences are the ones the decider's ruling actually turns on, not the implementation detail underneath them.

id.$comment: The record's address, when it is seated rather than passed as a fixture or a chat attachment.

name.$comment: The decision as a short noun phrase, as it would be said aloud to the decider.

decider.$comment: Who is being asked to rule, named the way they would recognise themselves — never an office slug or a repo path the decider would need this tree open to resolve.

status.$comment: IETF-style last call before canonization: a decision moves from proposed, to a final call for objection, to decided. A record with no status is proposed.

context.$comment: The forces at play that make a decision necessary, in plain language a decider with no access to the repository's state can read cold. Kept below the decider's altitude means kept ABOVE it here: the situation as it bears on the ruling, not the implementation underneath the situation.

options.$comment: The alternatives actually weighed, evaluated against what the context forces, per CMMI DAR. A record naming one option offers no decision, only an announcement — this is the exact shape of the bare yes/no line the requirement was raised against, and minItems 2 is what a validator can hold it to.

recommendation.$comment: Which option the carrier recommends, and why, per CMMI DAR's recommended solution. Optional: a record may reach its decider with the options weighed and no recommendation pressed.

decision.$comment: What was ruled, once status is decided. Absent while the record is still proposed or at last call.

consequences.$comment: What follows from deciding, stated for the options still live or the one chosen — benefits and costs both, per ADR's consequences section. This is what the decider is actually ruling on; it is where the decider's altitude is answered, and it must never smuggle in a consequence the decider cannot act on.

$comment-absences: No verified-by or closed-with: whether a decision was carried well is read off whether the decider could rule on it without opening the repository, not asserted by the record. No priority: the same ruling this glossary makes against requirement.schema.json applies here — priority without a decider is a feeling.
title: decision record
